additions.reason: The teaching's entire structure is built on establishing that the tzaddik's words share the essential nature of prophecy. The parallel is explicit and detailed: (1) the tzaddik speaks to his visitor — his words contain hidden hints; (2) the visitor does not understand the meaning at the time; (3) after returning home, events occur that make the meaning clear retroactively. The teaching then immediately says 'וְכֵן מָצִינוּ אֵצֶל הַנְּבִיאִים' (and so we find with the prophets), establishing that this is the same structure. The prophets' words are the paradigm; the tzaddik's words are the living continuation of that paradigm. דברי הצדיק and נבואה share the same essential nature: both are channels of hidden divine truth communicated in remez, both are understood only retroactively (lemafrea) after fulfillment. A bechina edge דברי הצדיק ↔ נבואה is missing from the dataset for Torah #186.

Remez is not the cause of prophecy or the tzaddik's words — it IS what they are. The bechina chain is: דברי הצדיק = נבואה (both are expressions of the same thing), and the shared nature of that thing is: רמז. רמז is the hub node of Package 1: it connects both concepts through shared essential quality. Polarity good: remez as a vehicle for divine truth is a positive spiritual phenomenon.

analysis_notes.note_on_bechina_language: Torah #186 uses structural-parallel bechina language rather than explicit formula-language like 'הוא בחינת' or 'נקרא'. The primary bechina formula here is 'וְכֵן מָצִינוּ' (and so we find) — used to equate two phenomena by showing they have the same essential structure. This is a legitimate bechina pattern in Likutay Moharan: when the Rebbe establishes that two things work the same way in every essential dimension, he is saying they share the same essential nature (bechina), not merely that one resembles the other (mashal). The key test: is the comparison saying 'A resembles B in some ways' (mashal) or 'A and B are expressions of the same underlying reality' (bechina)? In Torah #186, the teaching argues that the tzaddik's words ARE prophetic in essential structure — not merely like prophecy but the same phenomenon (a tzaddik IS a prophet of the living present). This justifies classifying דברי הצדיק ↔ נבואה as a bechina rather than a mashal.
analysis_notes.note_on_teaching_structure: Torah #186 is a short five-sentence teaching. Its structure: (1) Opening observation — miracles of tzaddikim from Kiev are revealed because the people there believe in tzaddikim (eitza: emunah → revealed miracles); (2) Mechanism explained — the tzaddik IS full of miracles; the believer focuses on his every word; returning home, he understands retroactively (lemafrea) that events fulfilled the tzaddik's hints; (3) Prophetic parallel — the same pattern with the prophets: prophecy in remez, not understood at the time, understood retroactively after fulfillment; (4) Daniel example — Daniel's hints about the end of redemption are sealed now, will be understood retroactively when Messiah comes; (5) Generalization — 'and so we find with many prophets.' The teaching's argument is: emunah (eitza-driver) → retroactive understanding (eitza-result), explained through the structural identity of tzaddik-speech and prophecy (bechina). The short length and primary eitza structure explains why the dataset captured this teaching mainly under one eitza edge.
